slides.title: TRAINING IN THE VEHICLE
slides.body:
The Flying Doctor is an important figure because is called to analyze issues on the vehicle and try to fix
them. Today we have a great variety of vehicles regarding the propulsion and they are different types:
- ICE (Internal Combustion Engine) Vehicles that have traditional engine (the combustion one);
- Hybrid vehicles, that have two kind of engine: combustion and electric engine;
- Electric vehicles that their propulsion is given only by electric engine;
So, It is important that Flying Doctor knows a great part of these typologies. But what are the
instrumentations used by Flying Doctor on the vehicle? In the first, we need the bridle.
We connect it to a particular plug of the vehicle: the EOBD, that
allows to communicate with the different ECUs. The EOBD plug
has 16 pins as reported in the imagine. Every pin is associated
at specific function. We can communicate with ECUs thank to
CAN network. We have different CAN networks on the vehicle
and some pins are dedicated to communication. In Fiat vehicles we have the CAN 1 on pin 6/14. These pins
are always the same and are regulated by the law, instead other pins of CAN communications, can change
and it depends by the vehicle. We have the CAN 2 on pins 12/13 and BH CAN on pins 3/11. We have also
the CAN 5 dedicated on Powertrain but their pins are not present on EOBD plug. In the other part of bridle
we have the DB9 (we can see them in the following imagines) that we can connect to laptop. The pins
dedicated to communications are 2 and 7.

slides.title: TOOLS USEFUL CANALYZER
slides.body:
Then, Flaying Doctor needs to the CANcase that is an hardware to interface with the vehicle.
In particular the DB9 are connected to CANcase. As mentioned before, there are different CAN networks
and they have different speeds. Every channel of CANcase has a transceiver that is very important to
transmit the messages. The transceiver can transmit within a range of speeds. Out of this range, messages
can not be sent, so for Flying Doctor, it is important to connect the right DB9 at the right channel of the
CANcase. In the end, Flying Doctor needs some tools to operate on the vehicle. We can outline what we
have told
There are different tools that the Flying Doctor can use depending the purpose of his visit.
Canalyzer works on the CAN network domain and it is used mainly to see the communication between the
different ECUs on CAN network. The tool has different functions, some of these are recording logs and
seeing how signals evolve to check if there is some issue on the vehicle.
Using Canalyzer it is necessary, in the first, to have the license and then to connect the CANcase to laptop.
After that we must:
- Choose the number of the channel using;
- Upload the DBCs for every channel. The DBCs are files that represent a database of ECU and we can
see all message in every ECUs in a specific CAN network and all signals in a specific message; Under
we can see how to add DBCs on Canalyzer. We go to “Analysis & Stimulation” and “Database
Management”.

slides.title: 3 - A ssociate the channel s of CANcase to Canalyzer ones and set the speed of networks. If on the trace we see the chan
slides.body:
- Associate the channels of CANcase to Canalyzer ones and set the speed of networks.
If on the trace we see the changing messages between ECUs, the association of channels will be correct and
we’ll see a green light on the CANcase. We report the correct exchanging of messages in the trace.
It is important underline that we can not see any message on trace if there is the SGW (secure gateway)
locked. It is an ECU installed on vehicle to protect it by people that are not allowed to connect to ECUs. To
Unlock the SGW , It will be necessary to use other tools. The previous diagram could be represented in this

slides.title: 4 INCA INCA is a tool used to see and read internal signal s of ECUs. In general , we can say INCA is able to see within
slides.body:
INCA is a tool used to see and read internal signals of ECUs. In general, we can say INCA is able to see within
the ECUs. Why can we analyze internal signals? When a new software is released to fix issues of previous
ones, some value of calibrations is changed. So with INCA it is possible to change those calibrations to adapt
the new software at the same vehicle and to avoid to make totally a new one. We can do it importing
calibration from reference page to the working page. For this, we can say INCA works in the calibration ECU
software domain. This operation can be made if we have a
development ECU. Otherwise, if we have a production ECU,
it is not possible to change values of calibrations with INCA,
so it is necessary to update the new software version on
ECU, flashing it. To do this operation we need an other
hardware, called ETAS. (picture on the left). With this
hardware we can connect two CAN networks, the supply
wire connected to the vehicle, the Ethernet network and a
particular wire called ETK. ETAS is connected to vehicle
thanking ETK and It is useful because it allows to
communicate with vehicle bypassing the SGW. We connect
the wire between the ETAS hardware and the EOBD plug
(We can see the scheme in the next page).
We have already said with INCA it is possible to change values of calibrations. It is allowed thanking some
particular calibration protocols, CCP and XCP . They are based about different communication protocols, CCP

slides.title: 5 (Can Com m un i cation Protocol) regards CAN messages, XCP (Extended Co m munication Protocol) regards extended CAN me
slides.body:
(Can Communication Protocol) regards CAN messages, XCP (Extended Communication Protocol) regards
extended CAN messages. Without these protocols, it is not possible to change values of calibration in real
time. It is possible to flash only the ECU. Of course when we speak about changing value, we are refering to
open ECUs.
CDA/DIANALYZER
CDA and Dianalyzer are tools used for the diagnosis. They work on diagnostic ECUs domain and there are a
lot of operation we can do, for example to read DTC (Diagnostic Trouble Code). DTCs represent the fault set
on ECUs and they are composed by three bytes. The first and second represent the component, the third
the symptom. DTC could be active, so the fault is present in vehicle at the moment, or stored, the fault is
not present anymore but the DTC is stored in the ECU memory. To have support with DTCs and diagnosis
there are some useful instructions. They are:
- RDI (Read data by Identifier). They are instruction give you informations about parameters of ECUs.
For example, we can send the RDI of engine speed to have the exact value. The diagnostic
command is 22.
- I/O Control. They are commands sent to actuator to perform a specific action. The diagnostic
command is 2F
- Routine. As I/O control, they are instructions sent to ECUs to perform a specific action. The different
with I/O is routine is not related only a single actuator and does not perform a single action but It
involves a serious of components performing different instructions. The diagnostic command is 31.
CDA
CDA is a powerful tool used for diagnosis. When we open the tool, CDA ask which CANcase are we using, so
we select the correct one.
Then we must select the CAN network associated to channel CANcase. After that, one of most
important thing to do is unlocking the SGW , otherwise, we will not be able to communicate with the
ECUs. When SGW will be unlocked we can start with the diagnosis. In ECU list there are blue and red
ECUs, the firsts are identified, the seconds with an exclamation mark, no and there isn’t
communication.

slides.title: 6 On the left we see a panel with different functionality. For example , the thunderbolt allows to flash ECUs with new s
slides.body:
On the left we see a panel with different functionality. For example, the thunderbolt allows to flash ECUs
with new software, under (the car with the arrow) it is possible to see the DTC of the all ECUs. Then the
panel indicated by blue arrow allows to make Scan Report, an important document where we can see all
DTCs of ECUs with their relative parameters, to understand which DTC could have set the fault. Selecting an
ECU, it will appear a new panel with several options.
Here the most important panel are reported:
1) Read/Write data: We can find a list of RDI. We select the RDI of our interest and in the panel on the
right there will be a list of parameters connected to RDI and it will be possible to read the value of
RDI requested.
2) DTCs: We can see the DTCs of that specific ECU. They will be active or stored. We remember that
stored DTC can be cancelled.
3) IO Control: We have a list of IO. We click on the I/O of our interest to send the command to actuator
4) On-Board Routines: As the I/O, we have a list of routines. Also here, selecting routines of our
interest, we will send the command to ECU.

slides.title: DTC MATRIX
slides.body:
5) PID Editor: In this panel, we have the same function of panel 1,3 and 4 but in the panel 5 we can
write manually the RDI/IO/Routine and see the positive or negative answer. We remember if the
answer is positive, we have the number of request plus 40. For example if we send the request of
RDI (22) the positive answer is 62. If the answer is negative, we’ll have 7F.
DIANALYZER
Dianalyzer is an other important tool used for diagnosis. It was made by FIAT. When we open the tool, we
must write our credentials and update the car file, that contains all the characteristics of the vehicle. After
that, we can see the main screen as reported.
On the left we have a list of
ECUs regarding a specific CAN
network. Selecting an ECU, in
the top of the screen we have
several panels. The first reports
the general command where we
can see the trace of the
messages. In the panel 2 we
find the general informations
about the ECU like SW number
and the HW number. In the
panel 3 DTCs are reported. We can find the code of DTC, the snapshot and the environmental parameters.
In the panel 4 we have RDI. There is a list of RDI, we can select one of them and see its parameters. In the
panel 5 we find the I/O control, as RDI by list we can select that of our interest. Panel 6 is dedicated at
PROXI, that it is a configuration file where we find all features of vehicle, for example if vehicle has the
adaptive cruise control. The body is the master and has the PROXI of all ECUs, In some vehicle also IPC has
the PROXI of the vehicle. Other unit controls receive the part of PROXI of their interest by the body. It is
important giving the right PROXI to the vehicle, otherwise the vehicle will set DTCs regarding PROXI.
Recalling the example of Adaptive Cruise Control, If the vehicle doesn’t have the ACC but it is present in the
PROXI, the vehicle will set DTCs about PROXI of ACC absent. Panel 7 is dedicated to Cyber Security. Here we
can unlock the SGW. In the end, in the panel 9, it is possible to update new software on ECU. We need three
files: IDX, PRM and BIN.
1) IDX file: It is an electronic label that contains all datas about software and hardware.
2) PRM file: It is a line guide to flash the ECU
3) BIN file: It is the software to flash the ECU.
The DTX Matrix is a powerful instrument used to execute the diagnosis. It is a table where all DTCs of the
ECU are reported. With the DTC Matrix, It is easier to understand what is the issue and how to fix it. We can

9 It is organized in several parts, Adas regarding ECUs connected to ACC system (Adaptive Cruise Control system) , Powet
slides.body:
system), Powetrain involves ECUs of the propulsion system, then we have body, interiors and Audio. We
have different CAN networks, the most important are C1, C2, BH and C5 (ePT network). We can see that the
ePT network connects only the ECUs of Propulsion. In the scheme It is represented by light blue line. We

BPCM and EVCU have the termination resistance, instead in the C1 BCM and EVCU have the termination
resistance. The resistances are the yellow rectangle inside the ECUs.

slides.title: EXERCISE
11 After that , we can use CDA to see if that fault could set some DTCs. We saw there were a lots of DTCs and only two r
slides.body:
After that, we can use CDA to see if that fault could set some DTCs. We saw there were a lots of DTCs and
only two reported the MIL on, so the fault could be connect to these two. One was on TBM and other on
PCM. This last was the P012D - Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Air Pressure Sensor 1 Circuit High. For the
presence of the MIL, the fault could be caused by the DTC of PCM, so we opened the DTC Matrix of PCM.
We saw among the possible causes “open circuit” or “short circuit” about a sensor. So we checked the
sensor of turbocharger and we saw it was disconnected. After connecting the sensor, we checked on CDA if
the DTC was still active and it was stored. Executing the clearing of memory DTC was cleared and the MIL
was off.
In general, It is better to make a Scan Report when the issue is present and after it was fixed. If it is difficult
to understand which DTC causes the problem, It could be useful to make a log and see if there is some
signal with a value unexpected.
